timeline_cost.notes: This is the timeline and government fee range to obtain approval of the four entitlements (CUA, ABC Type 41, health permit, building permit with change of use) when they are granted, not a time or cost to denial or withdrawal. The critical path is the CUA hearing (120–180 days from filing to Planning Commission decision in April 2022 practice) plus 30 days for the decision to become final, then the ABC investigation and referral review (60–120 days if unprotested; add 30–90 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required for an undue-concentration tract). The building permit and health plan check (21–60 days for DPH review, then 14–120 days for DBI permit issuance depending on plan quality) can overlap with the ABC timeline if construction drawings are ready when the CUA is approved. The health permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is complete) is the last approval before opening. Government fees: CUA application ~$2,700–$3,100 (2022 estimate), ABC Type 41 $1,000–$1,600, DPH plan check $828–$2,207, DPH permit to operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), business registration $55–$700, grease interceptor/FOG $0–$500, sign permit $300–$1,500. State business formation and tax registration (CA SOS $70–$150, seller's permit $0, EDD $0, EIN $0) and employee certifications (food safety manager $100–$250, food handler cards ~$50 for 5 employees, RBS training ~$75 for 5 staff) add roughly $300–$1,000. Private costs not counted here: attorney, architect, expediter, workers' comp insurance premiums, construction, lease, and music licences. The day range assumes a complete CUA application with no requested continuances, an ABC application filed immediately after CUA approval with no protests or PCN delay, complete building plans that pass review on first or second correction cycle, and inspections scheduled promptly.

records_summary: The records show 735 Jackson St is in the Chinatown Residential Neighborhood Commercial (CRNC) district where a restaurant with beer & wine is a conditional use requiring a Planning Commission hearing. The site history reveals a 2011 denial for a small self-service restaurant at this exact address, followed by two earlier approvals (2005 full-service restaurant referral, 1989 CUA for dim sum). The immediate block is extremely dense: 49 registered food or drink businesses and 22 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, with 4 bars in the count. Over the past 5 years within 1,000 feet, 8 of 10 dated use decisions were approved (80% approval rate, N=10), with 2 withdrawals and no outright denials in that window.
